'''Sneed Body Collard III''' (born 1959) is an American author.

On November 4, 2006, Collard received the Washington Post/Children's Book Guild Award, presented annually to "an author or illustrator whose total body of work has contributed significantly to the quality of nonfiction for children."<ref name=DCAward>{{cite web|url=http://www.childrensbookguild.org/nonfiction-award/past-winners/2006-winner|title=Washington Post-Children's Book Guild Nonfiction Award Winner 2006|publisher=Children's Book Guild of Washington DC|date=November 4, 2006|access-date=9 January 2014}}</ref>
In 2006, Collard also received the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) award for his science book ''The Prairie Builders: Reconstructing America's Lost Grasslands''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sbfonline.com/Subaru/Pages/PrairieBuilders.aspx|title= Excellence in Science Books:Winner! 2006 Middle Grades Science Book|publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|access-date=9 January 2014}}</ref>
Collard has written almost 100 books for young people, including ''Shep—Our Most Loyal Dog'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://childrenscrownaward.org/winners.htm|title=Triple Crown Award Winners (2008–2009)|publisher=Children's Crown Award Reading Program|access-date=9 January 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131117200105/http://www.childrenscrownaward.org/winners.htm|archive-date=17 November 2013}}</ref> ''Fire Birds: Valuing Natural Wildfires and Burned Forests'', ''Hopping Ahead of Climate Change: Snowshoe Hares, Science, and Survival'', and ''Dog Sense''. His picture book ''Border Crossings'' won the prestigious 2024 [[Orbis Pictus Award|Orbis Pictus award]] from the [[National Council of Teachers of English]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ncte.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/OP_Winners_2022-2024.pdf|format=PDF|title=Past Winners of the Orbis Pictus Award|website=Ncte.org|access-date=26 June 2026}}</ref>

He is also the author of an adult memoir, ''Warblers & Woodpeckers: A Father-Son Big Year of Birding'' (2018, Mountaineers Books), a professional development textbook, ''Teaching Nonfiction Revision: A Professional Writer Shares Strategies, Tips, and Lessons'' (Heinemann, 2017), the travel guidebook ''First-Time Japan'', and the humorous birding guide ''Birding for Boomers'', which won several awards and made the PNBA regional bestseller list.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mountaineers.org/books/books/birding-for-boomers-and-everyone-else-brave-enough-to-embrace-the-world2019s-most-rewarding-and-frustrating-activity|title=Birding for Boomers: And Everyone Else Brave Enough to Embrace the World’s Most Rewarding and Frustrating Activity|website=Mountaineers.org|access-date=June 26, 2026}}</ref>

He is a regular contributor to ''Montana Outdoors'', [[Bird Watcher's Digest]] (BWD), and other magazines for adults. His articles also have appeared in ''Environmental Action'',<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140110121212/http://connection.ebscohost.com/c/book-reviews/9512194379/book-reviews Environmental Action; May/Jun90, Vol. 21 Issue 6, p. 31], ''Web.archive.org''</ref> ''The Humanist'', ''Florida Wildlife'', ''Islands'', ''Cricket'', and ''Highlights for Children''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.highlightskids.com/|title=Highlights Kids|website=Highlightskids.com|access-date=June 26, 2026}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Collard has been a biologist, computer scientist, speaker, and author.

The son of biologists, Collard says that he fell in love with the animals at an early age, watching whales with his mother and searching for snakes, turtles, and alligators with his father.

Collard began writing after graduating with honors in marine science from the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He earned a master's in scientific instrumentation at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], after which he worked as a computer consultant for biologists.

As of 2026, Collard lives in Montana where he continues to write books and articles for both young people and adults.<ref name=RRTranscript>{{cite web|url=https://www.readingrockets.org/books/interviews/collard/transcript|title=Transcript from an interview with Sneed Collard|website=Readingrockets.org|access-date=9 January 2014}}</ref>
